data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 claims the panel wins only under a restricted definition of reliability (variance reduction), but then offers no evidence within a single evaluation that would distinguish genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance. The problem explicitly asks the respondent to 'identify what evidence within a single evaluation would distinguish a genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance that happens to track the right answer.' SRC_001's mechanism and counterconditions address variance and shared bias but never specify any intra-evaluation evidential criterion (e.g., item-level agreement, out-of-checklist probe, or calibration pattern) that separates real understanding from rote compliance, so it leaves the mandatory evidential task unaddressed.
